angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 714,484 km at 28.73 pc = 0.33 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: distance 28.726 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.007), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 28.726 +/- 0.201 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 34.6958 +/- 0.0287 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00), 1207.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 1.027 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: radius 1.027 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.404 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 714,484 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4543 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: effective temperature 4543 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.106) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114322: effective temperature 4543 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.106) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 218566 (pscomppars): spectral type K3V, from Turnbull 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015arXiv151001731T/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 218566 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.28 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 218566 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.45223, from Meschiari et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJ...727..117M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 218566 (pscomppars): age 8.5 Gyr, from Meschiari et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJ...727..117M/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, HD 218566: projected rotation speed 1.84 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2023A&A...676A..90R)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 4.79 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 13 published values span log g 4.02 to 4.81, across which the limb law changes by at most 1.0% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
